name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,180

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: University and public body featuring in verse by Indo-Chinese native

indicators.note: to feature in something is to appear inside it, so these parts sit within the verse-and-by pair

blocks.note: V is the standard abbreviation for verse
U is the usual abbreviation for university
a quango is a quasi-autonomous public body
X is the multiplication sign, read as 'by' in dimensions like 3 x 4

explanation.surface: A college and a government agency appear in a poem written by someone from Indochina.
explanation.walkthrough: U and QUANGO go inside V...X, giving VU QUANG OX. A quango is a British term for a semi-independent official body funded by government.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vu Quang ox, or saola, is a rare wild bovine found only in the forests of Vietnam and Laos.

clue.text: Festival coming up in park, as ever

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters run from bottom to top
the letters sit inside the words that follow rather than being defined by them

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of park, all of as and the start of ever

explanation.surface: A festival held every year in the park, as it always has been.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the hidden letters bottom to top to get VESAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Vesak is the Buddhist holy day marking the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and death.

clue.text: Short crack, ear-splitting, scattered or spread bees?

indicators.note: something short has been cut, so the word loses its final letter
scattered things are thrown about, so the letters of the hyphenated word are rearranged

blocks.note: a crack is a witty remark
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A short, deafening crack sends a swarm of bees flying in all directions.
explanation.walkthrough: The bees are not insects: a bee is a social gathering for shared work, and quilts are bedspreads, so the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Quilting parties are gatherings where neighbours sew bedspreads together, so they are bees devoted to making spreads.

clue.text: Foolish behaviour, carrying old uranium away from Axis

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so the first word wraps around the next two

blocks.note: antics are silly capers
O is the standard abbreviation for old
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Silly behaviour by someone carrying uranium away from the wartime Axis powers.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital A makes Axis look like the wartime alliance; here it is a plant's stem. ANTIC(O U)S.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany, anticous describes the side of an organ facing away from the stem's central line.

clue.text: See perfectly in grey-green light

blocks.note: GR is a dictionary abbreviation for grey
a green light is permission to go ahead, an OK

explanation.surface: Seeing clearly in the dim grey-green light of dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen ties grey to green, but the parts split as grey and green light. Grok comes from Heinlein's novel Stranger in a Strange Land.
explanation.definitionFit: To grok is to understand something intuitively and completely, which is seeing it perfectly in the mind's eye.

clue.text: Unknown article to drop in belly will make you no thinner!

definitions.note: a cryptic description standing for a noun: something that thickens

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the drop goes inside the belly

blocks.note: X is the classic unknown quantity in algebra
the indefinite article
tum is an informal word for stomach
to hang is to droop or drop down

explanation.surface: A mystery item you put in your stomach turns out to be no help with dieting.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads like a diet warning, but 'no thinner' means a thickener, which is what this food additive is. X AN T(HANG)UM.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanthan gum is a thickening agent added to sauces and dressings, so it makes a liquid anything but thinner.

clue.text: Decisive punches in quiet American scrap

indicators.note: the punches are placed inside the call for silence

blocks.note: sh is the call for quiet
knockouts, abbreviated KO, are the punches that end a fight

explanation.surface: A fight story: knockout blows landed in a quiet American brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrap looks like a fight, fitting the punches, but it means a tiny bit. S(KOS)H.
explanation.definitionFit: Skosh is US slang, borrowed from Japanese, for a small amount or little bit.

clue.text: So close to impromptu fencing, a black Caribbean tree

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept
to fence something is to enclose it, so the first word surrounds the next two

blocks.note: sic is Latin for so or thus
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the final letter of impromptu

explanation.surface: A swordsman's improvised bout of fencing, set against a black Caribbean backdrop.
explanation.walkthrough: S(A B)IC followed by U gives SABICU.
explanation.definitionFit: The sabicu is a leguminous tree of Cuba and the West Indies, valued for its hard timber.

clue.text: Head of OPEC, you organised fixer to annul the first energy commission

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
annulling the first one cancels it, so the earliest of those letters is struck out

blocks.note: the first letter of OPEC
ye is the old form of you
to run an event is to organise it
a determiner is one who fixes or settles something
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: The OPEC chief arranges for a fixer to cancel the first energy commission.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first E from DETERMINER to get DTERMINER. Oyer and terminer is Anglo-French for 'to hear and determine'.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission of oyer and terminer was a royal warrant empowering judges to hear and decide criminal cases.

clue.text: A hut on dry ground for submariner

indicators.note: something ground is crushed up, so the letters before it are broken and remade

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A hut on dry land is the place for a sailor from a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On dry ground' reads as one phrase about land; ground is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydronaut is someone trained to work in deep-sea vessels, a deep-diving crewman of a submersible.

clue.text: Corrupt Arab sent on hadj is denied a fruit

indicators.note: being denied something means going without it, so one A is withheld from the letters
to corrupt something is to twist it out of its proper form

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dishonest Arab pilgrim on the hajj is refused a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one A from the fodder before rearranging. The hadj (hajj) is the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca.
explanation.definitionFit: St John's bread is the carob pod, the legendary food of John the Baptist in the wilderness.

clue.text: Tawdry design that is evident in one's friends?

indicators.note: something evident in a group is seen within it, so the abbreviation goes inside

blocks.note: kith, as in kith and kin, are one's friends and acquaintances
sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for 'that is to say'

explanation.surface: Asking whether your friends' poor taste shows in their home decor.
explanation.walkthrough: KIT(SC)H. The question mark admits that the kitsch might belong to your friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch is showy, sentimental art or decoration of poor taste, so it is cheap, tasteless styling.

clue.text: Rookie vet keeping a horse turning over

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside
turning round means the pair before it is read backwards

blocks.note: to vet something is to check it
A as written, then H, slang for heroin, which is also called horse
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: An inexperienced vet holds on to a horse that keeps rolling over.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEC(HA)K + O. 'Turning over' looks like one phrase, but over is a separate abbreviation; an over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheechako, spelt chechako too, is Alaskan and Yukon slang for a newcomer or tenderfoot.

clue.text: Curses one heaps up, following tail of wicked old political saboteur?

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter
in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from the bottom
following means coming after, so the letter from wicked goes first

blocks.note: the last letter of wicked
drat is a mild curse
Roman numeral one
heaps means lots, many

explanation.surface: A wicked old troublemaker hurls a string of curses.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the letters bottom to top, and 'following' puts the last letter of wicked first.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamitard was a nineteenth-century political bomber, especially an anarchist or Fenian using dynamite.

clue.text: Bishop bringing to the surface, perhaps, establishment of dubious pretexts

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
unburying, digging up, is one way of bringing something to the surface

explanation.surface: A bishop digs up evidence, perhaps exposing a network of dubious excuses.
explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, where Algernon invents a sick friend, Bunbury, as an excuse to escape engagements.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunburying is inventing a fictitious person or reason as a cover for absence, so it means setting up dubious alibis.

clue.text: Hog, young, mostly, one raised in large country

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
the numeral is lifted out of the country and set above it, ahead in a down entry

blocks.note: a baby is a young one
Roman numeral one
Russia is the largest country by area

explanation.surface: A young pig, more or less, reared in a big country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' means the one in the country is lifted out and placed higher, which in a down entry is earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: The babirusa is a wild pig of Sulawesi whose upper tusks curve up through its snout.

clue.text: Lawyer after promotion conversing with others

indicators.note: after means the legal officer is placed second, behind the promotion

blocks.note: an ad, an advertisement, promotes a product
a DA is a district attorney in the US

explanation.surface: A lawyer, newly promoted, chatting with colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: Promotion suggests a career step; here it is advertising. Adda is a Bengali word, used in Indian English.
explanation.definitionFit: Adda is relaxed, lengthy group chat among friends, a Bengali social custom of informal talk.

clue.text: Refrain no longer from smashing vase, about due to be emptied

indicators.note: about means around, so the vessel goes round the emptied word
emptying a word removes its insides, so only its outer letters stay

blocks.note: fab, short for fabulous, means smashing, great
an urn is a kind of vase
the first and last letters of due

explanation.surface: Stop holding back from smashing the vase: the debt is about to be cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing vase' looks like breaking pottery, but smashing means great. FAB + UR(DE)N. 'No longer' marks an obsolete sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Faburden, an old form of fauxbourdon, was used in former times for a burden or chorus of a song.

clue.text: Spiritual father raised Jack the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means running backwards, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: raised means up
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, an AB or able seaman

explanation.surface: A priest brought up a jack in some card game the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: UP AB read backwards gives BAPU.
explanation.definitionFit: Bapu, Hindi for father, is the affectionate title given to Mahatma Gandhi as India's spiritual leader.

clue.text: Companion, note, regularly put on posh woman's cloak

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
put on means placed after, in an across entry

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
U means upper class, as in U and non-U
dame is an informal word for a woman
the first and third letters of note

explanation.surface: A friend, a musical note and a smart lady's cloak, like a fashion item list.
explanation.walkthrough: PAL + U DAME + NT. U for upper-class comes from a 1950s British essay on class markers in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A paludament was the military cloak worn by a Roman general, a scarlet mantle fastened at the shoulder.

clue.text: Reduced ships: after cutting one hundred, notice emperor upset

indicators.note: cutting something out removes it, so the hundred is taken away
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run upwards

blocks.note: to notice is to see
a czar was a Russian emperor
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: An emperor is upset to notice that his fleet has been cut by a hundred ships.
explanation.walkthrough: CZAR without C is ZAR; SEE ZAR read upwards gives RAZEES.
explanation.definitionFit: A razee was a warship cut down by removing its upper deck, so razees are ships lowered in size.

clue.text: Sort of skirt female medium's got out of curiosity

indicators.note: something got out has been removed, so that letter leaves the name

blocks.note: a ra-ra skirt is a short flounced skirt like a cheerleader's
Mavis is a woman's name
M is the abbreviation for medium, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A woman consults a spiritualist medium about a skirt, purely out of curiosity.
explanation.walkthrough: Medium wants to be a psychic, but it is the size label M; the 's is 'has'. MAVIS minus M gives AVIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rara avis, Latin for 'rare bird', is a person or thing so unusual it is a real oddity.

clue.text: With ends removed, protuberance has got to dip

indicators.note: removing the ends cuts off the final letter of each of the two following words

blocks.note: a hump is a rounded bulge
must means has got to

explanation.surface: A swelling has had its tip cut off and now must be dipped in something.
explanation.walkthrough: Dip looks like a verb at the end of a sentence; it is the noun, a sauce for dipping.
explanation.definitionFit: Hummus is a chickpea and tahini purée served as a dip with bread and vegetables.

clue.text: Little spray's brought up for techie

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a posy is a small bunch of flowers, plus the 's

explanation.surface: A small bouquet is handed up to someone who works with computers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stays with the word, so POSY'S read upwards gives SYSOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A sysop, short for system operator, runs a computer system or online forum, a technical role.

clue.text: Ultimate in scuttlebutt in literary gossip column

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of a word is its final one
in places the chosen letter inside the collection of gossip

blocks.note: ana is a collection of sayings, anecdotes or gossip about a person
the last letter of scuttlebutt

explanation.surface: The latest rumour turns up in a literary gossip column.
explanation.walkthrough: Gossip column sounds like a newspaper feature; the column is architectural. AN(T)A.
explanation.definitionFit: An anta is a square pilaster at the end of a side wall in classical architecture, a kind of pillar.

clue.text: French department assisted nine in English translation

indicators.note: translation turns words into a different form, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A French region's name, which was helped into English by nine translators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In English translation' reads as one phrase; in and English are fodder too.
explanation.definitionFit: Seine-Saint-Denis is a département in the Paris suburbs, an administrative region of France north-east of the capital.

clue.text: Stifling onset of rage, when one's no longer raising voice

definitions.note: an obsolete sense, marked by no longer

indicators.note: stifling something smothers it, so the following phrase wraps around one letter
the onset of a word is its beginning, its first letter

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
the first letter of rage
I for one, with the 's

explanation.surface: Holding back a fit of anger once you have stopped shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: A(R)S + IS. 'No longer' looks like part of the wordplay; it marks the old meaning of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody, arsis once meant the elevation of the voice on a stressed syllable, a sense now obsolete.

clue.text: Channel regulator putting blame on rant I'd broadcast

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so these letters are strewn into a new order
putting one thing on another places it after, in an across entry

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written
to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: A TV channel's regulator blames the station for a rant it broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Channel and regulator suggest TV and Ofcom; it is plumbing. Broadcast is the anagram signal, not the TV sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A drain trap is the U-bend in a waste pipe that holds water to block sewer gases, controlling the drain.
